highest_value_fixes: 1. scene-fix: Rebuild the night value hierarchy and contact integration. Preserve darker timber/stone midtones, localize lantern and candle pools, temper the beige veil, and give trainer/props consistent lighting and boot/base grounding. Prioritize both nave-forward_night_clear and both shrine night cameras on Medium and High. Make clear-day versus rain window light meaningfully distinct without adding rain inside the hall.

2. scene-fix: Author inhabited bays and structural joins. Retain the useful nave post/beam rhythm visible in B, resolve upper blue wedges/dark slits, refine post-floor/beam joints and avoid blocking door signs. Compose reception supplies, seating and shrine approaches into purposeful clusters with a clear central route and quieter floor values; broad room volume should remain grand without feeling vacant.

3. needs new art: Supply a coordinated portal/shrine identity set with actual dimensional arch profiles, readable biome emblems and purposeful shrine pedestals rather than identical doors, black infill and tilted lecterns. Add restrained timber joint/base detail and less repetitive material treatment where the current straight posts and tiled stone cannot carry landmark quality. The trainer silhouette is serviceable from the rear; these frames do not justify a new human model or a face verdict.
bar_a_world_fit_rationale: Keyart-world fit: NO for both arms at the requested quality bar. The cream plaster, natural timber, grey stone, teal cloth and blue/brown trainer are directionally compatible with a Meadows settlement; B improves authored nave silhouette and near/middle/far structure. However the vacant cobbled floor, repeated opaque windows, ordinary labelled doors and lectern-like shrine props do not yet convey the coherent, inhabited, welcoming landmark character of the reference. Judged palette, mood, composition and silhouette rather than painted pixel fidelity. Relative scale is broadly possible for a grand hall and human doorways, but furniture occupancy and weak contact make the 1.80 m trainer feel detached. All 26 full-size A/B pairs and the contact sheet were viewed; only isolated interior idle evidence is assessed.
bar_b_atmosphere_rationale: Same kind of game as Palworld: NO as a convincing finished visual presentation for either arm; only the broad third-person stylized adventure language is shared. The trainer has readable hair, jacket, collar, backpack and boots but looks miniature and disconnected in the oversized, repetitive space, especially when night haze affects scenery far more than the character. Face and animation appeal cannot be assessed from these fixed rear idle frames. Day views lack a strong directional/ambient light hierarchy, rain largely changes tint/value, and night turns into a uniformly pale beige room with bright circular floor spots. This does not deliver the warm/cool separation, layered depth or grounded subject presentation of the supplied shipping references or the requested Valheim atmosphere. High offers only a slight daytime contact improvement over Medium; neither preset solves the central defects. No performance, traversal, exterior or fullworld conclusion is inferred.
